tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local negative-control replay of the prior abstract claim/idempotency model. This replay removes exactly one assumption: atomicity of the uncommitted check plus effect mutation plus durable idempotency-marker commit. Serialized authority turnover is restored and retained; each authority has a distinct non-reusable identity; effect identity effect:E is stable; the durable marker persists once written. Two concurrent repair attempts under the same current authority A0 are permitted to interleave the uncommitted check, effect mutation, and marker write as separate steps. No public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, external coordinator, richer-mode arbitration, hosted compute, concrete transport, or optional second semantic leaf is modeled.

fixture.removed_assumption: atomic uncommitted-check plus effect mutation plus durable marker commit
retained_assumptions: durable marker persistence after marker write
counterexample_schedule: A0 is current; effect:E is uncommitted and its marker is absent.
Repair attempt R1 under A0 checks the marker and observes effect:E uncommitted.
Repair attempt R2 under the same still-current A0 checks the marker before R1 writes it and also observes effect:E uncommitted.
R1 performs effect:E but has not yet written the marker.
R2 performs effect:E before either attempt writes the marker.
R1 writes the durable marker for effect:E.
R2 writes the same durable marker; marker persistence now prevents later attempts but cannot undo the second already-performed effect.
fixture.duplicate_effect_search: A duplicate-effect schedule exists: both same-authority attempts pass the separated uncommitted check and both perform effect:E before either marker write linearizes.
fixture.authority_check: Current-authority-only ownership is preserved in this replay because serialized turnover keeps A0 current for both effect executions; the failure is duplicate suppression, not stale-authority execution.

observations: Removing only the atomic check/effect/marker assumption is sufficient to create a two-attempt duplicate-effect schedule even with perfectly serialized authority turnover.

Durable marker persistence after the fact is insufficient: the marker must participate in the same indivisible winner-decision/effect boundary, or the effect primitive itself must provide equivalent conditional idempotency.
This separates authority correctness from duplicate suppression: serialization protects who may act, while atomic conditional effect+idempotency semantics protect how many times the effect can occur.
inference: Within this exact abstract model, an atomic winner decision coupled to the effect and durable idempotency state, or a behaviorally equivalent conditional/idempotent effect primitive, is necessary for at-most-once execution under same-authority concurrent repair. This does not establish availability of such a primitive on any concrete Chat-exposed repository/API transport, crash consistency, fork exclusion, infinite-turnover liveness, or real multi-claimant behavior.
unresolved_children: A concrete allowed zero-cost quota-independent Chat-exposed transport exposing an atomic conditional mutation or behaviorally equivalent idempotent effect primitive remains unverified.
Crash consistency if failure occurs between the external effect and durable marker remains unverified unless the effect and marker share one transactional boundary.
Fork exclusion and real multi-claimant contention remain unverified.

The next negative control should test marker persistence loss/replay across recurrence while restoring atomic conditional commit semantics, to distinguish crash/reconstruction safety from same-run race safety.
